1.title: Deployments, Configuration and Self-Healing Workloads
1.text: Welcome to Module five: Deployments, Configuration and Self-Healing Workloads. It covers the exam area Workloads and Scheduling. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, and every task was run on a real cluster, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do four things. Understand application deployments and how to perform rolling updates and rollbacks. Use Config Maps and Secrets to configure applications. Understand the primitives used to create robust, self-healing, application deployments. Practice with ten hands-on labs worth sixty-two points.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Workloads and Scheduling (fifteen percent). Practice in this module: ten labs, sixty-two points, about sixty-seven minutes. Exam format: performance-based tasks in a live terminal, scored on the final cluster state. Validated on: Kubernetes version one point thirty-seven point zero.

1.title: Which workload object for which job
1.text: Which workload object for which job. Deployment. Use it for: stateless apps. Pod names: random suffix. Key facts: owns Replica Sets; rolling updates and rollbacks. Stateful Set. Use it for: apps that need stable identity or storage. Pod names: name-zero, name-one,... Key facts: needs a governing (usually headless) Service; ordered start. Daemon Set. Use it for: one Pod per node (agents, log shippers). Pod names: random suffix. Key facts: ignores replicas; needs tolerations for tainted nodes. Job. Use it for: run to completion. Pod names: random suffix. Key facts: completions, parallelism, restart Policy must be Never or On Failure. Cron Job. Use it for: Jobs on a schedule. Pod names: Job per run. Key facts: cron schedule; suspend pauses it. Exam tip: A Daemon Set needs a toleration for the control plane taint if it must run on the control plane node.

1.title: Which workload object for which job, continued
1.text: Which workload object for which job. Create fast: kube control create deployment api the image flag set to engine X alpine the replicas flag set to three, kube control create job, kube control create cronjob tick the image flag set to busy box the schedule flag set to or ten -- date. A Daemon Set and a Stateful Set have no create command: generate a Deployment with the dry run flag set to client dash o yaml and edit kind and fields.

1.title: Rolling updates and rollbacks
1.text: Rolling updates and rollbacks. A Deployment replaces Pods gradually. strategy dot rolling Update has two knobs, each a number or a percentage. max Surge. Meaning: how many extra Pods may exist during the update. Default: twenty-five percent (rounded up). max Unavailable. Meaning: how many Pods may be missing. Default: twenty-five percent (rounded down). Exam tip: A stuck rollout keeps the old Pods running: undo it with kube control rollout undo.

1.title: Rolling updates and rollbacks, continued
1.text: Rolling updates and rollbacks. max Unavailable zero with max Surge two means "never lose capacity, add two new Pods first" (Lab five point two). strategy dot type Recreate stops all old Pods first (downtime). The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: Rolling updates and rollbacks, continued
1.text: Rolling updates and rollbacks. kube control create deployment names the container after the image ( engine X ). kube control set image needs that container name: read it with kube control get deploy web dash o json path dot spec dot template dot spec dot containers dot name. A bad image keeps the old Pods running (with max Unavailable zero rounding on three replicas) while new Pods show Err Image Pull or Image Pull Back Off. The update is stuck, not failed. rollout undo fixes it (Lab five point one). Only changes to the Pod template (image, env, probes) create a new revision. Scaling does not.

1.title: ConfigMaps
1.text: Config Maps. A Config Map holds non-secret settings as key or value pairs. Three ways to create. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: ConfigMaps, continued
1.text: Config Maps. Three ways to use. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: ConfigMaps, continued
1.text: Config Maps. Mounted Config Maps update inside the Pod after a short delay; environment variables do not update until the Pod restarts. Read the task for "from the Config Map, not hard-coded": a hard-coded value fails the check.

1.title: Secrets
1.text: Secrets. A Secret is like a Config Map for sensitive data. Values are base sixty-four encoded, not encrypted (anyone who can read the Secret can decode it). The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study. Exam tip: A Secret is base sixty-four encoded, not encrypted; mount a Secret volume with read Only true.

1.title: Secrets, continued
1.text: Secrets. Use as env with secret Key Ref or as a volume secret secret Name db creds. Mount with read Only true when the task says so (Lab five point four). Quote values with! in the shell with single quotes.

1.title: Self-healing primitives
1.text: Self-healing primitives. Replica Set (via Deployment). keeps the desired number of Pods; replaces deleted or failed ones. restart Policy ( Always, On Failure, Never ). the kubelet restarts failed containers ( Always is the Pod default; Jobs need the other two). Liveness probe. if it fails, the kubelet restarts the container. Readiness probe. if it fails, the Pod is removed from Service endpoints (not restarted). Startup probe. holds off liveness and readiness checks for slow starters. Exam tip: A liveness probe restarts the container; a readiness probe only removes the Pod from the Service endpoints.

1.title: Self-healing primitives, continued
1.text: Self-healing primitives. Pod Disruption Budget (P D B). limits voluntary disruptions (node drains, evictions): min Available or max Unavailable for the Pods its selector matches; kube control create poddisruptionbudget web pdb the selector flag set to app web the max unavailable flag set to one; kube control drain waits instead of evicting a Pod that would break the budget (Lab five point one zero). Resource requests or limits. scheduling and protection (Module six). Probe types: http Get (path and port), tcp Socket, exec (command), G R P C. Common settings: initial Delay Seconds, period Seconds, timeout Seconds, failure Threshold.

1.title: Self-healing primitives, continued
1.text: Self-healing primitives. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: Self-healing primitives, continued
1.text: Self-healing primitives. Break-and-fix pattern (Lab five point nine): a liveness probe pointing at the wrong port makes the container restart in a loop ( R E S T A R T S climbs; kube control describe pod shows "Liveness probe failed"). A readiness probe on the wrong port leaves the Pod Running but zero slash one Ready forever. Different symptoms, same fix: correct the probe and let the rollout replace the Pods.

1.title: StatefulSets in short
1.text: Stateful Sets in short. A Stateful Set gives Pods stable names ( db-zero, db-one ) and, with a headless Service ( cluster I P None ) named in service Name, stable D N S: db-zero dot db. namespace dot svc dot cluster dot local (Lab five point six). Pods start in order and stop in reverse. Storage ( volume Claim Templates ) is covered in Module ten.

1.title: Jobs and CronJobs in short
1.text: Jobs and Cron Jobs in short. completions is how many successful Pods are needed, parallelism how many run at once, backoff Limit how many retries before failing. The Pod template must have restart Policy Never or On Failure. A Cron Job's schedule is five fields ( minute hour day of month month day of week ); or ten is every ten minutes.

1.title: Lab 5.1: rollback stuck update
1.text: Lab five point one: rollback stuck update. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about six minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. In the namespace roll, the Deployment web (three replicas) was updated to an image tag that does not exist, and the update is stuck. Roll the Deployment back to the previous working revision and make sure all three replicas are Ready. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

1.title: Lab 5.1: rollback stuck update, Solution
1.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n roll rollout history deployment web. Then kube control dash n roll rollout undo deployment web. Then kube control dash n roll rollout status deployment web the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

1.title: Lab 5.2: rolling update strategy
1.text: Lab five point two: rolling update strategy. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about six minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. In the namespace strat, the Deployment api runs four replicas of engine X alpine. Change its rolling update settings to max Surge two and max Unavailable zero, then update the image to engine X stable alpine and wait for the rollout to finish. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

1.title: Lab 5.2: rolling update strategy, Solution
1.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n strat patch deployment api dash p spec strategy rolling Update max Surge two, max Unavailable zero. Then kube control dash n strat set image deployment api engine X engine X stable alpine. Then kube control dash n strat rollout status deployment api the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

1.title: Lab 5.3: configmap env volume
1.text: Lab five point three: configmap env volume. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about seven minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. In the namespace cfg, create a Config Map app config with the keys L O G L E V E L debug and color blue. Create a Pod cfgpod (image busy box one dot thirty-six, command sleep three thousand six hundred ) that. gets the environment variable L O G L E V E L from the Config Map key of the same name (not a hard-coded value), and. mounts the whole Config Map as files in the directory slash E T C slash app. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

1.title: Lab 5.3: configmap env volume, Solution
1.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n cfg create configmap app config the from literal flag set to L O G L E V E L debug the from literal flag set to color blue. kube control dash n cfg apply dash f -. The manifest comes next, as shown on the screen. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

1.title: Lab 5.3: configmap env volume, Solution, continued
1.text: Lab five point three: configmap env volume, Solution, continued. Run volume Mounts. Then - name conf, mount Path slash E T C slash app. Then volumes. Then - name conf. Then config Map name app config. Then Y. Then kube control dash n cfg wait the for flag set to condition Ready pod slash cfgpod the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then kube control dash n cfg exec cfgpod -- sh dash c echo L O G L E V E L cat slash E T C slash app slash color.

2.title: Lab 5.4: secret env file
2.text: Lab five point four: secret env file. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about seven minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. In the namespace sec, create a Secret db creds with username admin and password S three cret exclamation mark. Create a Pod dbclient (image busy box one dot thirty-six, command sleep three thousand six hundred ) that gets the environment variable D B P A S S from the key password of the Secret, and mounts the Secret read-only at slash E T C slash db. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 5.4: secret env file, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n sec create secret generic db creds the from literal flag set to username admin the from literal flag set to password S three cret exclamation mark. kube control dash n sec apply dash f -. The manifest comes next, as shown on the screen. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 5.4: secret env file, Solution, continued
2.text: Lab five point four: secret env file, Solution, continued. Run volume Mounts. Then - name creds, mount Path slash E T C slash db, read Only true. Then volumes. Then - name creds. Then secret secret Name db creds. Then Y. Then kube control dash n sec wait the for flag set to condition Ready pod slash dbclient the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds.

2.title: Lab 5.5: daemonset
2.text: Lab five point five: daemonset. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about seven minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. In the namespace agents, create a Daemon Set logger (image busy box one dot thirty-six, command sleep three thousand six hundred ) that runs one Pod on every node, including the control plane node (which has a taint). Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 5.5: daemonset, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. kube control dash n agents apply dash f -. The manifest comes next, as shown on the screen. Then kube control dash n agents rollout status daemonset logger the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then kube control dash n agents get pods dash o wide. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 5.6: statefulset
2.text: Lab five point six: statefulset. This task is worth seven points, and you should plan about eight minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. In the namespace data, create a headless Service db (port eighty) and a Stateful Set db with two replicas of engine X alpine that uses this Service as its governing service. The Pods must be named db-zero and db-one, and db-zero must be reachable by the D N S name db-zero dot db dot data dot svc dot cluster dot local from inside the cluster. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 5.6: statefulset, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. kube control dash n data apply dash f -. The manifest comes next, as shown on the screen. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 5.6: statefulset, Solution, continued
2.text: Lab five point six: statefulset, Solution, continued. Run ---. Then api Version apps slash version one. Then kind Stateful Set. Then metadata name db. Then spec. Then service Name db. Then replicas two. Then selector match Labels app db. Then template. The remaining lines are on the screen.

2.title: Lab 5.7: job cronjob
2.text: Lab five point seven: job cronjob. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about six minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. In the namespace batch, create a Job report (image busy box one dot thirty-six, command echo done ) that must complete three times, running two Pods in parallel. Also create a Cron Job tick (image busy box one dot thirty-six, command date ) that runs every ten minutes. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 5.7: job cronjob, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. kube control dash n batch apply dash f -. The manifest comes next, as shown on the screen. Then kube control dash n batch create cronjob tick the image flag set to busy box one dot thirty-six the schedule flag set to or ten -- date. Then kube control dash n batch wait the for flag set to condition Complete job slash report the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 5.8: add probes
2.text: Lab five point eight: add probes. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about seven minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. In the namespace probes, the Deployment site (two replicas, engine X alpine ) has no health checks. Add to its container. a readiness probe: H T T P get or on port eighty, initial Delay Seconds three, period Seconds five. a liveness probe: H T T P get or on port eighty, initial Delay Seconds ten, period Seconds ten. All replicas must be Ready afterwards. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 5.8: add probes, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n probes patch deployment site dash p spec template spec containers name engine X, readiness Probe http Get path or, port eighty, initial Delay Seconds three, period Seconds five, liveness Probe, and so on. Then kube control dash n probes rollout status deployment site the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 5.9: fix liveness
2.text: Lab five point nine: fix liveness. This task is worth seven points, and you should plan about seven minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. In the namespace flaky, the Pods of the Deployment app (two replicas, engine X alpine ) restart again and again. Find out why and fix the Deployment so that both replicas are Ready and stay running (restart count zero on the new Pods). Do not remove the liveness probe. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 5.9: fix liveness, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n flaky describe pod dash l app app then pipe to grep dash i -A two liveness probe failed then pipe to head -five. Then kube control dash n flaky patch deployment app the type flag set to json dash p op replace, path slash spec slash template slash spec slash containers slash zero slash liveness Probe slash http, and so on. Then kube control dash n flaky rollout status deployment app the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 5.10: pod disruption budget
2.text: Lab five point one zero: pod disruption budget. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about six minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. In the namespace pdb, the Deployment web (three replicas, label app web ) exists. Protect it during voluntary disruptions such as node drains: create a Pod Disruption Budget named web pdb that selects the Pods with app web and allows at most one of them to be unavailable at a time. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 5.10: pod disruption budget, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n pdb create poddisruptionbudget web pdb the selector flag set to app web the max unavailable flag set to one. Then sleep four. Then kube control dash n pdb get pdb web pdb. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Recall Check 1
2.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Which command undoes the last rollout? Answer: kube control rollout undo deployment or name. Question two. What do max Surge and max Unavailable control? Answer: The extra Pods allowed and the Pods allowed to be missing during a rolling update. Question three. What happens when a failed liveness probe is detected? And a failed readiness probe? Answer: Liveness: the container is restarted. Readiness: the Pod stops receiving Service traffic.

2.title: Recall Check 2
2.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Are Secret values encrypted? Answer: No, they are base sixty-four encoded. Question five. Does an environment variable from a Config Map change when the Config Map changes? Answer: No; only after the Pod restarts. Mounted files do update. Question six. Why does a Daemon Set not appear on the control plane node by default? Answer: The node has a No Schedule taint; add a matching toleration.

2.title: Recall Check 3
2.text: Recall check three. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question seven. Which Service type does a Stateful Set's service Name normally point to? Answer: A headless Service ( cluster I P None ). Question eight. Which restart Policy values are allowed in a Job's Pod template? Answer: Never or On Failure.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. Update: set image, rollout status slash history slash undo, max Surge or max Unavailable. Stuck rollout: old Pods stay; new Pods Err Image Pull; fix with rollout undo. Config Map use: env dot value From dot config Map Key Ref, env From, volume (files). Secret: base sixty-four, secret Key Ref, volume with read Only true. Probes: liveness restarts; readiness removes from endpoints; startup delays both. Daemon Set: tolerate the control plane taint to reach all nodes. Stateful Set: name-zero, headless Service, stable D N S. Job: completions, parallelism, restart Policy Never or On Failure. In the next module, we continue the course.
